# ledger_occurrence (Data Source)

These are derived reports, not configuration. One occurrence of a commitment with its payment state. Use it to find the occurrence a deferral plan or manual payment hangs off.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One occurrence, to find the occurrence a deferral plan or manual payment attaches to.
data "ledger_occurrence" "one" {
  id = "01JD3Y4C8V9M2Q7W5R6T0XZ001"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The occurrence identifier (a ULID).

### Read-Only

- `amount` (Attributes) The amount due. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--amount))
- `cancelled_at` (String) When it was cancelled, or null.
- `cancelled_reason` (String) out_of_range, terms_change or commitment_deleted, or null.
- `commitment_id` (String) The commitment it belongs to.
- `created_at` (String) When it was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `due_date` (String) The due date, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `month` (String) The month it falls in, YYYY-MM.
- `payment` (Attributes) The payment state. status is what Ledger shows: it is derived_status from the evidence unless the person set an override; the override and its reason are kept separately so the two are never confused. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payment))
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `version` (Number) The optimistic-concurrency version.

<a id="nestedatt--amount"></a>
### Nested Schema for `amount`

Read-Only:

- `amount` (String) Exact decimal amount as a string, in the scale Ledger stores it. Never a floating-point number.
- `currency` (String) ISO 4217 currency code of amount.


<a id="nestedatt--payment"></a>
### Nested Schema for `payment`

Read-Only:

- `bank_evidence_count` (Number) Of those, the ones matched to a bank transaction.
- `derived_status` (String) The status derived from recorded evidence alone, ignoring any override.
- `evidence_count` (Number) Payments counted as evidence, bank and manual.
- `grace_until` (String) The end of the creditor's grace period, or null.
- `leeway` (String) not_recorded, unknown, none, period or deadline, or null.
- `manual_evidence_count` (Number) Of those, the ones the person recorded by hand.
- `outstanding_amount` (Attributes) What is still owed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payment--outstanding_amount))
- `overpaid_amount` (Attributes) What was paid beyond the amount due. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payment--overpaid_amount))
- `override` (Attributes) The person's status override, or null when there is none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payment--override))
- `paid_amount` (Attributes) The amount paid, in the currency of the occurrence. Evidence in another currency is not converted here: see unconverted_currencies. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payment--paid_amount))
- `shortfall_amount` (Attributes) What is missing against a tolerance-accepted payment. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payment--shortfall_amount))
- `status` (String) paid, partially_paid, upcoming, due, overdue, not_recorded or cancelled.
- `timing` (String) upcoming, due, overdue or not_recorded, or null.
- `unconverted_currencies` (List of String) Currencies of payment evidence that could not be counted because no conversion applies.
- `within_grace` (Boolean) True while the occurrence is late but inside the grace period.

<a id="nestedatt--payment--outstanding_amount"></a>
### Nested Schema for `payment.outstanding_amount`

Read-Only:

- `amount` (String) Exact decimal amount as a string, in the scale Ledger stores it. Never a floating-point number.
- `currency` (String) ISO 4217 currency code of amount.

Read-Only:

- `currency` (String) ISO 4217 currency code of amount.


<a id="nestedatt--payment--override"></a>
### Nested Schema for `payment.override`

Read-Only:

- `applied` (Boolean) Whether it currently decides the status.
- `previous_status` (String) The status it replaced, or null.
- `reason` (String) Why the person set it.
- `set_at` (String) When it was set.
- `status` (String) paid or unpaid.
